suggestions.rationale: Scalp discoid lupus erythematosus can produce cicatricial (scarring) alopecia through inflammatory injury centered on hair follicles and permanent follicular/scarring damage. This relationship is limited to documented scalp DLE with a distinct clinical or dermatopathologic diagnosis of scarring alopecia; it does not treat nonscarring hair loss, alopecia areata, or systemic lupus erythematosus as interchangeable phenotypes.

pathwayIntelligence.causalChain: Documented inflammatory scalp DLE → perifollicular/appendage injury and scarring damage → cicatricial alopecia when permanent follicular loss is clinically or histopathologically established.
developmentQuestions: Are active or prior discoid lupus lesions documented on the scalp in the same anatomic distribution as the hair loss?
Is the hair loss diagnosed as cicatricial/scarring alopecia rather than alopecia areata or another nonscarring alopecia?
Do dermatology examination, trichoscopy, or scalp biopsy findings support DLE-related perifollicular inflammation and follicular destruction?
What is the chronology from active scalp DLE to permanent scarring and hair loss?
Are lichen planopilaris, central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia, traction, infection, treatment injury, or another scarring alopecia cause present?
issuesToResolve: Scarring alopecia is a phenotype-specific complication of scalp DLE and should not be inferred from cutaneous DLE at non-scalp sites.
Clinical or dermatopathologic confirmation is needed to distinguish cicatricial alopecia from nonscarring lupus-associated hair loss and unrelated alopecia disorders.

evidenceGaps: Dermatology documentation confirming discoid lupus involvement of the scalp
Clinical, trichoscopic, or histopathologic confirmation of cicatricial/scarring alopecia
Anatomic and temporal correlation between DLE scalp lesions and permanent hair loss
Assessment of competing cicatricial and nonscarring alopecia diagnoses
Dermatology opinion when the individual attribution remains uncertain

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-9 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Discoid lupus erythematosus can progress to systemic lupus erythematosus in a clinically meaningful subset of patients. Require established discoid lupus erythematosus and separately established systemic lupus erythematosus meeting appropriate classification or diagnostic criteria. Do not infer SLE from DLE alone. Preserve ANA and other autoantibody findings, hematologic abnormalities, systemic manifestations, family history, and other classification criteria as independent diagnostic evidence. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Authoring registers this relationship only as the bounded association the located cutaneous lupus literature supports, with the phenotype boundary stated first: a 2026 systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 25 studies reports depression as one of the commonest discoid lupus comorbidities at pooled prevalence 38.8 percent, with a significant case-control association at OR 2.21 (95 percent CI 1.71-2.85) alongside anxiety (OR 2.40, 1.40-4.11), hypothyroidism (OR 2.55, 1.79-3.61), hypertension (OR 2.22, 1.91-2.58) and cardiovascular disease (OR 3.85, 1.67-8.88), its own authors cautioning that most association analyses rest on a LIMITED NUMBER OF STUDIES (PMID 41849118); a 2019 cross-sectional analysis of a population-based cohort of 106 patients with primary chronic cutaneous lupus (predominantly Black, metropolitan Atlanta) reports moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms in 26.4 percent (PROMIS), three to five times the local general population, with multivariate determinants of perceived staff disrespect (OR 2.35, 95 percent CI 1.06-5.17) and low emotional support (OR 0.48, 0.35-0.66) rather than any disease-severity variable (PMID 30877492); and a 2022 cross-sectional path analysis of 121 patients with primary chronic cutaneous lupus reports moderate-to-severe depression in 30.6 percent with stigma associated with depression (adjusted b = 0.44, 95 percent CI 0.23-0.66) and social isolation mediating the relationship (PMID 35953237). The registered claim is the narrowest these anchors jointly permit: that discoid lupus is associated with a substantially elevated burden of depressive morbidity at the pooled prevalence and odds the anchors report, with NO anchor diagnosing persistent depressive disorder specifically and the dominant multivariate determinants being psychosocial rather than inflammatory.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of depression is established for any individual: NO located anchor diagnoses persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) at all - the meta-analysis pools depression outcomes of mixed definition and the two cohorts measure PROMIS depressive SYMPTOMS - so the corpus's persistent-depressive-disorder target is NOT met by any anchor, and ON THE QUALIFIED-HUMAN REVIEWER'S ELECTION OF 2026-09-29 THIS EDGE LANDS AGAINST THE GENERAL depressive-disorder WINDOW with the chronicity-defined window left UNAUTHORED and preserved in docs/batch-91-discoid-lupus-persistent-depressive-disorder-held-edge.json; the cohort evidence places the dominant determinants in the psychosocial domain (perceived disrespect OR 2.35, emotional support OR 0.48, stigma adjusted b = 0.44, social isolation as mediator), so the located literature supports a pathway from visible scarring, dyspigmentation and healthcare experience to depressive morbidity rather than a demonstrated direct inflammatory effect on mood; both cohort analyses are cross-sectional (the second a path analysis, which cannot establish temporal order), so reverse and reciprocal readings stand; the meta-analysis itself cautions that most association analyses rest on few studies. Individual claims require independently established discoid lupus and separately diagnosed depressive disorder with documented chronicity, exclusion of systemic lupus neuropsychiatric involvement, of corticosteroid and antimalarial treatment effects, of disfigurement-related adjustment disorder and of pre-existing psychiatric history before any attribution.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized psychosocial-circadian pathway rather than a direct inflammatory one: visible scarring alopecia and dyspigmentation carry stigma, social withdrawal and healthcare-interaction harm (the multivariate models' dominant determinants), which sustain depressive arousal, while a systemic inflammatory contribution (interleukin and interferon-axis effects on monoaminergic signaling) remains possible especially where systemic lupus co-travels (22.0 percent pooled SLE prevalence in the same meta-analysis); whether any individual's depression runs through the visible-disease pathway, the inflammatory pathway or a shared substrate remains hypothesized until the dermatologic, systemic and psychiatric chronology is read together.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Held at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at meta-analysis and cross-sectional-cohort class with two scope boundaries carried as controlling limitations. FIRST, the TARGET ELECTION recorded at the reviewer's direction: the corpus pair named Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) and NO located anchor diagnoses it - the anchors measure mixed-definition depression and PROMIS depressive symptoms - so the qualified-human reviewer elected on 2026-09-29 to land the edge against the general depressive-disorder window it actually evidences, the claim window is depressive morbidity in discoid lupus, and the persistent-depressive-disorder window REMAINS UNAUTHORED and is preserved with this election in docs/batch-91-discoid-lupus-persistent-depressive-disorder-held-edge.json; a reviewing clinician must separately establish any persistent-depressive-disorder phenotype before that window is claimed. SECOND, the dominant determinants in both cohorts are psychosocial (stigma, discrimination, support) rather than disease-activity variables, so the edge must not be read as evidence of a direct autoimmune-to-mood pathway. POPULATION BOUNDS: both cohorts are primary chronic cutaneous lupus (skin-confined, predominantly discoid), predominantly Black and female, in one US metropolitan area; the meta-analysis pools 25 studies of mixed design with most association analyses on few studies. The registry already carries depressive-disorder's very many incoming windows, so this edge adds one more mood window rather than a new mechanism class; the parallel-targeting question is NOT incremented here because the evidence class (visible-disease psychosocial morbidity) is distinct from the other primaries pointing at this target and no duplicate route is created.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: NO located anchor diagnoses persistent depressive disorder, which is why the corpus's chronicity-defined window is NOT authored and this edge claims only depression-general morbidity; all designs are cross-sectional (one a path analysis) with no temporal order; the dominant multivariate determinants are psychosocial rather than disease-activity variables; the meta-analysis cautions most association analyses rest on a limited number of studies and reports moderate variability for depression prevalence in sensitivity analysis; and both cohorts are single-metropolitan-area, predominantly Black, predominantly female, skin-confined primary CCLE populations, bounding extrapolation to systemic lupus and other demographics.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Systemic lupus neuropsychiatric involvement (the meta-analysis pools 22.0 percent SLE comorbidity) rather than skin-confined discoid lupus
Corticosteroid and antimalarial treatment effects on mood
Disfigurement-related adjustment disorder rather than a depressive disorder
Pre-existing psychiatric history and social determinants (employment, insurance, support) that dominate the cohort models
Hypothyroidism comorbidity (OR 2.55 in the same meta-analysis) as an endocrine mediator of mood symptoms
